Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{PS}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{SQ}=b,$ and $\overset{\to }{PT}=c.$ Find $\overset{\to }{QT}$ in terms of $a,b,$ and $c.$
question.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $Q$ to $T$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,$ and $c.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{QT}=\overset{\to }{QS}+\overset{\to }{SP}+\overset{\to }{PT}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14212914/assets/f728becaa8903fc0aa17ea9d15dd7199447dd70eff5b4a3d2be5982f1eeca8a5.png)

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{QS}=-b,\,\overset{\to }{SP}=-a,\,\overset{\to }{PT}=c.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14212914/assets/055bb2c63c42defaa9f624f20b8ad92dd80f3d34b0d689def859b34785318749.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{QT} & =\overset{\to }{QS}+\overset{\to }{SP}+\overset{\to }{PT} \\  & =-b+(-a)+c \\  & =c-a-b.\end{aligned}
$$
